view.rationale: Q2 revenue and Adj. EBITDA missed the preview's arithmetic floor and management cut FY Adj. EBITDA guidance materially, which outweighs the positive refinancing extension and liquidity improvement; higher CAC and near-term softening in demand point to deceleration.

Management cut FY ARR and revenue guidance and reported a Q2 ARR print below the preview, while renewal rates weakened and management announced headcount cuts — a guidance-driven negative for a stock priced for the ARR guide.

Record orders/backlog, a clear EBITDA beat and margin expansion, strong free cash flow, accelerated synergy capture, and a raised FY26 guide (higher low end) with no control issues — a clean relief-plus-upgrade print against a beaten-down valuation.

Material Q2 revenue shortfall and a steep FY guide cut (midpoint down ~15%) plus a push of cash‑flow breakeven into 2027 outweigh modest positives (better-than-expected quarter cash flow and diagnostics traction); the impairment is one‑time but the underlying demand and guide reset are structurally negative.

Revenue was roughly in line with the analyst base-case but management withdrew FY26 guidance and agreed to a material Hercules paydown that cuts pro forma cash, raising refinancing/dilution risk — modest operational beats (Cinvanti/Aponvy) don’t offset the guidance withdrawal and cash hit.

Revenue and EPS beat vs the pre-release yardstick and management raised FY sales and nudged up the margin floor; however higher post-deal leverage, weaker YTD cash flow and the stock's pre-print run-up cap upside, so the print is clearly positive but not unambiguously transformational.

Cash exited the quarter materially above the note's $20–22M estimate ($23.9M) and enrollment, Novo supply deal and patent allowance were reiterated — providing relief to the beaten-down stock — while runway language still implies additional financing for the full readout.

Revenue topped consensus and backlog printed a strong sequential build to $246.1M with management reaffirming FY guidance and reporting best-in-years operating cash flow and markedly lower net debt — but adjusted EBITDA was slightly softer and the stock entered the print priced for perfection, so upside should be muted.

Management cut FY27 revenue and adj. EBITDA guides and trimmed FCF, which overwhelms the positive SA contract acceleration; the stock came in priced for perfection so the lowered guide and Q1 EBITDA miss should drive a materially negative reaction. The SA acceleration and large enterprise wins are longer-term positives but do not offset the near-term guidance/FCF hit.

Q2 delivered a slight revenue beat and, more importantly, a meaningful upgrade to FY26 revenue and profitability targets (revenue growth to 13–15% and ~70% non-GAAP op income growth) alongside >$10M royalties and a large NPU customer — all positives versus the pre-print base, though the stock was priced richly into the print.

Quarter tracked the July 31 pre-announcement (revenue roughly inline, GM miss already disclosed, guidance reiterated), but orders/backlog came in below the bull bogey and a large portion of backlog sits beyond Q3; improved cash and EBITDA are positives but likely won’t offset skepticism, given the prior run-up and control issues.

The 10-Q numbers were public ahead of the call and the call confirmed the expected items (ETH accumulation, Galaxy fund, repurchases, June RDO); no new mNAV-linked buyback policy or material guidance was introduced, so the market is likely to treat this as narrative-only and react neutrally.

Strong Auvelity demand and early ADA traction (266k TRx, quantified prescriber activations and improved access) and a larger-than-expected cash balance were offset by a revenue slight miss and materially higher SG&A with management guiding Q2 SG&A to plateau at ~$208M — a negative for near-term operating leverage on a narrative stock.

Results and FY guidance were largely as-previewed: Q2 came in essentially inline to the company's cadence and consensus, and management delivered the expected Idaho Falls sale details and reiterated FY26 (ex-Idaho) guidance — removing a key tail risk but not materially improving the H2 bridge. The print is a modest positive given reduced leverage risk, but upside remains contingent on a quantified H2 plan or capital-allocation actions at close.

Large TONMYA revenue and total-product revenue materially exceeded the thin consensus (and the preview's base), showing clear commercial traction; however, higher operating spend and an unchanged runway into early Q2'27 leave dilution risk intact, so the print is positive but not unambiguously transformative.

Strong quarter: GMV +18.1%, revenue +22% and a materially higher take rate (6.47%) drove an EBITDA and EPS beat and pushed TTM adj. EBITDA above the $25M run-rate. However management flagged the Virginia-driven demand as temporary and gross margin compressed, and the stock went into the print with a bullish setup, so the market reaction should be positive but measured.

The quarter showed a large continuing-ops revenue and adj. EBITDA miss and management materially cut FY revenue/EBITDA guidance after deconsolidating the transportation businesses; modest positives (strong divestiture multiple, proceeds earmarked for debt paydown, improved leverage) do not offset the guide cut and H2 execution risk.

Q1 topped the guide/consensus with stronger revenue, EPS, a material new duty-free agreement and a new customer (Urban Outfitters), but management guided Q2 gross margins lower—dampening some of the upside for a stock that had been re-rated.

Q2 came in meaningfully above consensus and management materially raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance while reporting outsized WHS margins and large customer prepayments — a clear acceleration of the H2/2027 story that the market is paying for.

Fee-related earnings and margins beat the note's range, AUM and fee-paying AUM came in above expectations, and the large SpaceX mark / credit secondaries close materially improve the forward picture — but much of this setup was already anticipated and the stock sits near highs, so the market reaction should be modestly positive.

Top-line and EPS beat, and OCF improved, but adjusted EBITDA missed the house, student starts collapsed to 1%, and management merely reiterated FY guidance while materially raising capex — the guidance/capex disappointment and start weakness outweigh the beats.

Revenue beat the whisper and management raised FY adj. EBITDA materially while also boosting cash gross-margin guidance; the modest revenue trim (phasing out low-margin resale) tempers the print but the guidance raise on the key EBITDA metric drives a positive reaction.

Company delivered record revenue and record adj. EBITDA, and it lifted FY imaging and EBITDA guidance — all positive vs the preview — but much of the beat-and-raise was already priced into a high-multiple, run-up stock and digital-health ARR remains shy of the 'comfort' mark, limiting upside.

Operational execution beat the base-case: synergies ahead of schedule, lower capex and drilling efficiency, and first CCS revenue — but adjusted EBITDAX came in below the company Q2 guide and management did not accelerate buybacks (instead buying a pipeline), so the print is mixed and likely valued as a mild disappointment vs. the bullish narrative.

Refinancing of the $170M bridge with a $380M five-year term loan and better-than-expected operating results (Adj. EBITDA $50M, same-store NOI/margin beat, occupancy inline at 87.8%) remove the biggest near-term risk and justify an upside re-rate; management also committed to beginning FY-2027 FFO guidance (a positive governance change).

Company maintained FY guidance and delivered +40% YoY EBITDA, helped by 45Z credits and higher D3 RINs, but revenue missed consensus, EBITDA landed below the implied quarterly run-rate and production decelerated; liquidity also declined materially, leaving credibility questions for H2.

Revenue and profitability missed the pre-release yardstick (traffic headwinds persisted), which is the dominant negative; debt refinance and an accretive AI tuck-in remove a major balance-sheet overhang, limiting downside.

Revenue, consumables, flow-cell units and gross margin materially beat the guided/expected range and management nudged the FY midpoint higher — a clear operational upside — but the company still exits the quarter with limited runway and no removal of the existential financing question, so upside is meaningful but not unambiguous.

Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance (relief vs. a cut) but the quarter showed a material revenue and EBITDA miss, a sharp international decline and a cash draw to $43.9M — leaving the equity dependent on a sizeable H2 recovery. Mixed signals produce a slightly negative-to-neutral expected reaction.

Top-line came in meaningfully below Q1 consensus (−~8%), OCF swung to an $11.3M use and net bank debt rose to ~$99.7M — negatives that outweigh the reassuring adjusted gross margin (20.2%) and the reaffirmed FY27 guide. Overall a modestly negative outcome versus expectations.

Revenue missed materially (-5% YoY to $23.3M) and management walked back Q4 breakeven to a softer positive-FCF target while cash fell sharply to $5.3M — these are negative, unpriced items; cost cuts and G&A savings were bright spots but insufficient to offset the signal damage.

Revenue and Commerce Media Solutions materially exceeded the preview (CMS $30.5M, >$125M run rate) with outsized margin expansion (CMS margin 34%, consolidated gross margin ~29%), but liquidity/going-concern risks remain and the stock was priced-for-perfection, capping upside.

Attruby and total revenue materially exceeded consensus and the launch trend held/extended, reinforced by positive RWE and kidney-protection data and a concrete PDUFA date — offset only by an infigratinib timing slip and a rich pre-print valuation. Net is a constructive print but not a blowout versus a high bar.

The print delivered a modest revenue beat and a small FY26 raise — outcomes the market was leaning toward — plus upside in underlying gross margin and an acceleration in growth and a pulled-forward delirium launch; however the raise was modest, part of the margin headline was one-time, EPS slightly missed and cash declined, and the stock arrived priced-for-perfection, so the reaction should be only modestly positive.

Cash printed at the high end of the modeled range ($47.1M) and burn/R&D came in lighter than feared while the early-Q4 pivotal timeline and runway into early 2027 were reaffirmed (management also said no planned raise before pivotal) — removing the immediate financing overhang and making this a modestly positive, not transformational, print.

Modest P&L misses (revenue and adj. EBITDA) plus materially worse balance-sheet optics — $51.6M cash, revolver maxed and no FY guidance — create acute refinancing risk; the stock ran up into the print so this outcome is likely punished.

Q2 materially beat consensus on both revenue and adjusted EPS, with pro‑forma systemwide sales growth and clear momentum into Q3; however the stock went into the print near the highs on a favorable read‑across, and management provided no new guidance, limiting the unambiguous upside.

Big liquidity relief (cash $30.2M and ATM expansion) removes the existential overhang the market feared, but the quarter materially missed revenue/GM and management raised cash-burn guidance — liquidity wins dominate near-term, but execution concerns remain.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded the low bar embedded in consensus while management signed the Sea Ray deal and — crucially — upsized/refinanced the credit facility, materially reducing the ATM equity risk; some GAAP net income uplift came from one-offs but underlying operating beats and liquidity relief justify a constructive near-term reaction.

Mixed quarter: slight revenue miss and SDC delivery/backlog reversal on a richly valued stock offsets a clear AOI/margin beat and faster-than-expected debt paydown; no FY guidance given, so commentary rather than numbers will drive the tape.

Company exceeded the expected revenue and delivered materially better-than-anticipated margin/adjusted EBITDA and EPS while reaffirming guidance; the recent $109M offering and high multiple temper but do not erase the sizable operational upside.

Small revenue and EBITDA beats and a positive FCF print were offset by a sharp Multiplatform EBITDA deterioration and a Q3 midpoint (~$200M) that is below the ~$230M the note said is necessary to make the $800M full‑year bridge credible; management reaffirmed the $800M guide but left the H2 bridge unresolved.

Revenue and a large FY EBITDA raise materially beat the base case, but the quarter was dominated by ~$45M of payer settlements (quality issue) and cash is tight at $21M — so the print is positive but tempered by one-time items and liquidity risk.

Revenue beat and a raise to FY growth (15–16%) plus roughly breakeven gross margin and sharply lower cash burn are positives, but much of the opex improvement included a ~$37M one-time recovery and Texas proceeds remain unconfirmed, so underlying progress is more muted.

Revenue and backlog materially exceeded the preview (revenue $5.6M vs ~$4.7–5.15M and backlog ~$42.5M vs ~$16M), and management provided FY26 revenue framing that implies a combined midpoint well above consensus — clear constructive fundamentals — offset modestly by EPS being driven by non‑operating mark‑to‑market and elevated acquisition-related opex.

Revenue missed and management cut FY revenue guidance meaningfully, but adj. EBITDA came in positive and the EBITDA guide was maintained; much of the margin/EBITDA improvement was driven by a $5.3M tariff refund, so the one-off nature and the guidance cut on a stock that ran up into the print point to a negative stock reaction.

A transformational, multi-billion-dollar 20-year frontier AI lab lease (191 MW) plus a Corsicana full-site LOI, sizable liquidity and interim financing materially de-risk Riot's data‑center pivot and should drive a strong rerating despite a larger GAAP loss and some mining/recurring-lease shortfalls.

The company did what the note flagged as the key downside — it withdrew FY guidance — but the cash balance (~$30.4M) and international/Liquifix strength were not catastrophic and some negatives (revenue miss, PRS pilot failure, wider loss) were already contemplated. Overall this is a relief/neutral print with downside risks retained.

Huge revenue beat and a sharply raised sales guide drove a constructive headline, but a below-guide gross margin, a sequential backlog decline, and Memphis ramp costs make the print two‑sided — net positive given the stock was beaten down, but dependent on management's H2 margin bridge.

The quarter beat revenue and EPS and management materially raised FY operating income while providing a clear plan (cash + undrawn facility) to address the 2027 converts — removing a major tail risk — but ARR/D&R growth softened and Q3 ARR guide drops to ~812M, and the stock went into the print priced for perfection, leaving the signals mixed.

Revenue missed consensus materially, but management raised/repositioned FY26 revenue guidance midpoint above street and gross margin/adj. EBITDA held ~in line; backlog and book-to-burn are stronger-than-feared, offsetting the quarter miss and weak liquidity.

Management delivered the material deal disclosures the market wanted (Insitu confirmed profitable with >$200M rev and positive FCF), Q2 revenue materially beat consensus and adj. EBITDA came in at the low end of guide while Q3 guidance was maintained — these reduce execution and burn concerns and should re-rate the name, though some upside is tempered by the prior run-up into the print.

Slight revenue miss and higher-than-expected operating spend dent a richly priced narrative, even as sizable government awards, backlog growth and a low-cost $1.15B convertible strengthen the commercial story and liquidity. Because the stock came in priced-for-perfection, the modest miss + cost pressure favors a below-median reaction despite the positive backlog/finance news.

ACV reaffirmed FY guidance and delivered an EBITDA beat / record EBITDA-per-unit, but revenue came in just below the practical consensus bar and unit/ conversion metrics showed meaningful stress (price dislocation). The mix of an operational profitability beat plus clear unit-headwind and a CFO transition produces a mixed reaction — slightly negative-to-neutral near term.

Company delivered an operational beat (adj. EBITDA well above the high end) and raised FY26 guidance, with margin expansion and stronger cash — while registrations/enrollment were broadly inline and Q3 shows a modest timing shift, so the print is clearly positive but not a blowout.

Revenue and adj. EBITDA missed the pre-release build and management gave no update on the strategic review (the primary market driver), while AUM and net client inflows were surprisingly strong — a mixed print that should pressure the stock given the takeover run-up.

Q2 results were operationally solid (EBITDA and EPS beat, NDR and biopharma wins) but management trimmed FY26 revenue guidance midpoint and narrowed the range, which is the dominant driver for this stock; guidance downtick outweighs the quarter's positives given the company's valuation and the market's focus on forward bookings. Expect a negative to mixed market reaction.

Very large revenue beat and a modestly raised FY adj. EBITDA range, plus ahead-of-schedule Base Electron recognition, bond repurchase and a new $50M buyback, should drive a materially positive market reaction; offset by a large noncash warrant/SAR charge and lingering governance/legal overhang that limits upside from being unambiguously maximal.

Asset-sales (Watkins, Brasada) and a large SpaceX MTM gain meaningfully bolstered liquidity and NAV dynamics, but the restaurant business showed weaker traffic and a large $45M impairment plus no Q2 buybacks and further deployment into sports — a mixed but net-positive print versus the feared bear case.

Top-line and ATS profitability modestly beat the note's base case, but management warned Q2 was exceptional and guided to a sequential revenue decline into Q3. Given the stock's run-up (priced for perfection), the combination of a beat with a softer near-term guide and weaker Media/macro metrics should produce a muted-to-negative reaction.

Q2 delivered solid profitability (net income and adj. EBITDA exceeded the guide) and retail rollout progress, but the company gave softer Q3 revenue/margin guidance, reported a sizable FCF draw from inventory build and continued sequential subs decline — guidance outweighs the beat. Net effect is a modestly negative next-day reaction.

Revenue and underlying product traction (Truth API >10 customers) and a stronger-than-feared balance-sheet (gross financial assets $1.9B; ~$400M+ unencumbered) materially reduce the existential convertible-put risk, even though GAAP loss was larger than our model due to non-cash crypto marks and litigation-related expense.

Revenue materially beat the guide and accelerated; contribution ex-TAC roughly met the bar and adj. EBITDA beat, plus strong product/CTV metrics (Direct Access >80%, Outcomes adoption). Much of the good news was priced in, and the newly issued Q3 revenue midpoint is slightly below the note's higher revenue expectation.

Revenue came in roughly inline with the pre-print yardstick and management broke out Monovate (showing meaningful volume growth), which relieves the worst-case narrative; however payments revenue was slightly below the note's base-case and heavy one-time integration/transaction costs muted EBITDA and GAAP loss, and no material forward revenue guidance was provided.

Strategic-review progress (management saying the process is in later stages) and a record subscription attach rate materially de-risk some downside vs. the bear case, but guidance remains withdrawn and no cash/margin detail was provided, leaving substantial binary risk.

The print materially advanced the strategic pivot: CPG run-rate was upgraded sharply to $35–40M and management received an LOI to sell U.S. restaurants, while FY26 revenue guidance was reaffirmed — these positives outweigh the EPS miss, higher debt draw, and COGS mix pressure. Net: a clear de-risking of the pivot and improved forward narrative should drive a positive re-rating.

Material revenue and adjusted-EBITDA beats plus a meaningfully higher FY and Q3 revenue/EBITDA guide — against a large short base — should drive a strong upside move, even though margins are structurally lower and cash flow was negative this quarter.

The FDA issued an Additional Information letter requiring an SIR alignment meeting (raises delay/uncertainty around the ~Aug 22 de novo readout) while management also increased H2 cash burn guidance to ~$8M/quarter, pushing financing risk forward; revenue was immaterial ($21k) and no named U.S. orders were disclosed. These factors materially worsen the key regulatory and cash-runway catalysts the market was watching.

The quarter showed a materially worse operating result (negative adj. EBITDA and a cash-flow swing) versus the note's base case, but management delivered two sizable positives (lowered Turtle Creek cost / earlier COD and a larger forward-sales/contracts book plus favorable capacity pricing) and committed to non-dilutive funding — a mix that should leave the market disappointed on near-term profitability but grudgingly reassured on the long-term project path.

Revenue met the company's pre-announced $18.5M floor (so not a beat vs the meaningful yardstick) while gross margin and adjusted EBITDA materially outperformed expectations and revenue visibility (70% locked) improved — guidance was reiterated. That combination should elicit a modestly positive, but not euphoric, market response given the reverse-split/liquidity overhang and prior credibility concerns.

Revenue was roughly in line with the preview, but product gross margin moved from deeply negative to +14%, management reported strong order flow (~$45M YTD) and pushed an upbeat H2/profitability outlook — while the GAAP improvement was materially driven by one-time investment gains and a tax benefit.

Top-line and Adjusted EBITDA materially beat the pre-release yardstick, Honey Birdette comps stayed double-digit and licensing returned to growth while net-debt showed a clear path down; the one notable negative is a large, fixed-price share repurchase that could slow deleveraging. Overall this is net-positive vs expectations for a beaten-down stock.

Revenue and, critically, gross margin materially beat the guidance/consensus and adjusted EBITDA swung to a healthy positive; Q2 revenue guide is above the ~$78M level the model needed. Offsets: large one‑time GAAP charge (non‑recurring), a trimmed Q2 adjusted‑EBITDA guide, ongoing tape supply constraints and a sizable resale overhang temper upside.

Revenue came in inside the company guidance ($109.4M) with revenue/ unit up and June OR improving to 95.7% (positive), but adjusted EBITDA missed materially and the combined-entity guide implies ~97% OR and delayed synergies; the large Hansen & Adkins deal (and convertible financing) increases scale but also leverage and execution risk, leaving a mixed-to-slightly-negative read.

Modest revenue and considerably stronger-than-forecast adjusted profitability/margin vs the note's conservative model, but no FY guidance reinstated and heavy cash burn/operating cash outflow keep solvency concerns front-and-center.

Q2 revenue missed both consensus and the company's prior guidance and management cut FY revenue/adj. EPS below the previously expected low end; India launch was delayed to H1 2027. Adjusted EPS was inline and Prism.io device/scan traction was a bright spot, but the guidance cut and customer/recruiting weakness dominate the near-term outlook.

Large FY26 guide cut (~21% at midpoint) combined with an outright revenue and EPS miss and worsening net charge-offs (52%) materially undercuts the prior back‑half recovery narrative — this should trigger a strongly negative near‑term reaction.

Revenue materially beat the pre-release yardstick and management delivered the first formal guide (Q3 $87–93M) showing an accelerating Quake consolidation; GAAP net loss widened on largely one-time acquisition costs but underlying adjusted EBITDA improved.

Q2 revenue printed roughly in-line with the guide while Q3 revenue guidance midpoint came in above the Street — a positive — but the apparent Q2 margin beat was aided by a nonrecurring tariff refund and management guided materially lower gross margins for Q3. Given the stock was priced for perfection, the one-time nature of the margin beat plus guidance compression outweigh the modest upside in the Q3 revenue guide.

Management reaffirmed the FY26 guide (the single biggest risk) and delivered materially stronger-than-expected free cash flow, early synergies and slightly-better leverage, offsetting a mild EBITDA/revenue miss and weaker normalized organic growth; overall this supports a modestly positive reaction but not a re-rating toward the rejected bid.

Big y/y revenue decline and wider losses/EBITDA drive a negative read, partially offset by a key regulatory approval, a stronger cash balance after a capital raise and progress toward launch; commercial economics remain unclear so upside is uncertain.

Quarter landed essentially in management guidance (revenue at high end, EBITDA in range) while management reaffirmed FY guidance, provided a constructive Q3 guide implying a meaningful sequential ramp, and disclosed additional financing tranches — collectively a modestly positive relief/confirmation print for a heavily narrative-driven microcap.

Q2 results largely met the low bar the Street had set (revenue inline) while profitability (Adj. EBITDA, EPS) materially beat; however management trimmed the top end of FY revenue and called out airway/inventory destocking — for a high-multiple, low‑float name guidance tone outweighs the quarter's beats.

Q2 reported revenue was essentially inline and adj. EBITDA materially beat, but management cut FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance meaningfully below consensus — the guide undermines the valuation floor. Weak demand metrics (active clients down, GSV decline, AI automation accelerating) reinforce the negative read despite the quarter's margin beat.

Headline EPS massively beat due to a Transchem warrant re-measurement (one-time), but underlying business disappointed: Q2 TTV collapsed to $169M, cash fell to $50.7M and the company now needs ~ $2.1B in H2 to hit a maintained $2.5B target — a mathematically steep ask. Conditional Q4 adj. EBITDA break-even and higher strategic-asset marks offer limited relief.

Q2 was essentially in-line on revenue but beat on adj. EBITDA and showed stronger ad/Korea performance and strategic IP moves; however the modest Q3 constant-currency guide (0.7–3.3%) and hedged 'double-digit' wording undercut the acceleration narrative and should drive a negative tape.

Top-line materially beat (above the company's high end) and FY revenue guidance was nudged up, but management cut gross-margin guidance and cash flow weakened — mixed signals that should produce a modestly positive near-term reaction but capped upside.

A large $337M pretax CM charge and disclosure of roughly $500M of near-term project cash burn forced a formal cut to FY guidance (EPS midpoint to ~$4.05), which should drive a negative mechanical reaction; underlying metrics (record backlog, 1.6x book-to-burn, International growth) and management's excl.-charge reaffirmation limit longer-term damage.

Revenue came in just below the company's Q2 guidance floor (a formal miss) which is the headline negative, but product-level metrics (record Vevye revenue, strong AIHESO units/pricing) and a maintained FY guide temper the sell-off; signals conflict so expect a modestly negative reaction.

Underlying profitability and EPS materially beat and management provided concrete Savannah River economics and faster deleveraging, but revenue missed and FY26 revenue guidance was cut while FY27 headwinds were increased — with the stock having run up into the print the market is likely to punish the revenue/guide deterioration despite the earnings beat.

Quarter delivered stronger-than-expected organic growth and an EPS beat, management raised FY organic growth and materially quantified / expanded Nexus scope (bigger, multi-site ramp), and the company reiterated AOI/EPS ranges while advancing leverage progress — all de-risk the re-rating narrative.

Quarter mostly matched the preview: cash and R&D stepped up as restarts were real, but EPS/net loss missed consensus and management explicitly said an incremental ~$30M is needed to complete Phase 3 — highlighting likely future dilution and capping upside.

Material cash beat and a raise to FY26 adj. EBITDA to ~$15M (vs prior $14M) are the headline positives and beat the base-case; however the GAAP EPS beat looks driven by one-time accounting items while Q3 EBITDA declined, so the print should produce a modestly positive relief rally rather than a large re-rate.

Material revenue miss and management pushed the bulk of contracted ARR conversion into 2027 (undermining the H2 ramp the market needed), while improved gross margin and pro‑forma cash mitigate but do not offset the hit to near‑term growth.

Management reiterated the critical 'substantially enrolled by year-end' language, initiated the alternate-dosing study and slightly beat the cash midpoint — all largely in line with the preview. With the stock priced for perfection and a tight short float, the print should be a modestly positive but not large surprise.

Q2 delivered a clear operational beat (revenue ~$30M, adj. EBITDA ~$5.8M and +520bp gross margin) and management reaffirmed FY26 guidance, which eases near-term execution concerns; however materially worse-than-expected GAC conversion cost estimates ($40–60M) and no GAC production in 2027 limit upside and preserve a left-tail financing/capex risk.

Orders/backlog and ALP strength were as expected or slightly better, but revenue, consolidated adj. EBITDA and EPS missed the note's yardstick and the key FCEP normalization metric fell short of the ~$9M threshold; liquidity remains thin and no quantified upside guidance was given.

Two high-leverage milestones landed (a fifth Stage‑3 customer added ahead of schedule and an in‑place material supply/licensing agreement) plus steady foundry progress and healthy cash — these narrative wins should drive a materially positive reaction despite only inline financials.

Q4 EPS materially beat, but $0.31 of the beat is a disclosed one-time IEEPA refund; critically, management initiated FY27 guidance (midpoint $12.50) above street consensus and authorized a large $5B repurchase increase—offsetting a revenue miss ($63.7B vs ~$65B expected) and tamping sell-side fears.

Quarter and metrics (utilization, rev/HP, adjusted EBITDA) broadly met the preview; guidance was raised to the mechanical $103–108M the note expected. The GAAP EPS miss was driven by anticipated transaction costs, while adjusted results and leverage/deployment upside were modest positives.

Quarter materially missed the EBITDA and revenue bar that the note flagged as the covenant pivot; management cut Engage guidance and initiated a Digital strategic review, and EPS was hit by a valuation allowance — all driving a strongly negative re-pricing despite a secured amendment and some debt paydown.

Q2 delivered a modest revenue beat, materially higher gross margin and positive adjusted EBITDA plus a $7.6M ATM raise that meaningfully bolstered cash — all positives vs the preview — but management tightened the FY revenue range and warned of choppier H2 and a mix shift away from recurring session revenue, tempering upside for a stock that ran up into the print.

Modest revenue beat and a small raise to the low end of FY guide, plus a sizable $6M AP corrections order and larger-than-expected NearLab 2H contribution, materially de-risk the 2H bridge; AVCAD remains excluded (a single negative). The stock is richly positioned, so the reaction should be positive but not extreme.

Adj. EBITDA came in essentially inline/slightly ahead and the company reaffirmed FY EBITDA guidance while providing stronger liquidity, lower leverage and a clearer H2 growth cadence; offsetting this was a trimmed occupancy outlook (quality of recovery concern). Net is a modestly positive, mixed print.

Adjusted EBITDA modestly exceeded the pre-call bar (~$80M) and management materially raised FY26 FCF, while revenue and pounds processed disappointed and the EBITDA range was tightened (top end removed). Given the stock was priced for perfection, this mix should produce a modestly positive but not runaway reaction.

Management cut FY26 revenue range and reported a larger-than-expected EBITDA loss and cash burn; a small HEMOBLAST revenue disclosure and expanded sales footprint are positives but are outweighed by the guide trim, $5M distribution fee, deteriorating margins and liquidity squeeze.

Revenue slightly beat the note's realistic whisper and subscription/customer metrics (retention 94%, net revenue retention 124%, customers +24%) are constructive, but gross margin compressed and adj. EBITDA missed, and no formal forward guidance was provided — net: modestly positive reaction.

Quarter beat consensus modestly and margins expanded; management raised FY26 above street midpoint (to $880–900M / $3.05–3.25), confirming demand and freeing capital deployment — but near-term Q3 guidance shows some sequential slowdown, tempering the upside.

MG beat revenue and adjusted EPS/EBITDA, delivered record Q2 adj. EBITDA and expanded margins, raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance, and showed materially improved cash flow and leverage — a clear upside vs the pre-release base case.

Q2 headline beat was driven by a one-time revenue-timing/lease treatment in Private Cloud and management left FY guidance unchanged, so the underlying quarter is essentially inline; that said, a signed 30 MW AMD definitive agreement and asset-backed financing for the first tranche materially de-risks the 2027 AI optionality, yielding a modestly positive next-day reaction.

Q2 missed materially on both revenue (-8% y/y vs modeled +2.5–4%) and adjusted EBITDA (down to $13.7M vs model ~$26M), driven by >50% drop in turnaround revenues. Management did deliver a larger-than-expected $20–35M structural cost program but merely reaffirmed FY guidance while saying results will sit toward the lower half, which together make this a net negative for the equity.

Revenue and adj. EBITDA both missed the preview/consensus and management cut FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance materially below the prior guide, citing weaker demand and project delays — negatives that outweigh steady liquidity, buybacks and Nokē milestones. The stock went into the print exposed to an H2 margin ramp; the guide cut and organic weakness make that ramp less credible, pointing to a sizable negative reaction.

Top-line came in slightly better than my model (Q3 sales down ~6% vs my −8% est.), but adjusted operating profitability disappointed (EBITDA declined materially Y/Y) and liquidity weakened (cash below my prior $10–11M view and America reopening delayed). The quarter contains a few operational positives (lease savings, NYNY efficiency and a new MGM deal) but the miss to the margin / cash story dominates for this low‑liquidity, legally‑levered name.

Revenue was inline with the guide/consensus, but adj. EBITDA marginally beat to double-digit margin, management issued a constructive Q3 guide and — critically — launched a backstopped $125M rights offering that materially de-levers the balance sheet; these offset the stock’s pre-print run.

Q2 adj. EBITDA materially beat the preview ($60.7M vs $56–58M) and management kept the $245M FY midpoint while adding near-term FID color (sub‑6x build multiple) and more Williston activity — positives that offset a meaningful capex raise to $100–120M and a looming Piceance MVC step‑down. Given the name was priced for the H2 ramp, this is a constructive but not runaway print.

Clinical and enrollment metrics were reiterations or better-than-expected, opex and burn came in meaningfully below the preview — but cash of $6.9M and an explicit need for more capital (runway only to year-end) leaves solvency/dilution risk unresolved. Mixed signals on funding + small float favor a muted-to-negative near-term reaction despite good clinical news.

Underlying HE + Rail performance was better-than-feared (revenue and adj. EBITDA beat), and management de-risked Rail via contract exits, but adjusted EPS and free cash flow missed and the headline GAAP revenue was distorted by large, pre-announced one-offs. Stock is priced for perfection, so the mixed print with weaker EPS/FCF should produce a modestly negative reaction.

Results largely tracked the preview: production beat the guide and LOE came in meaningfully below guidance while realized hedge losses landed near the expected ~$55M; cash strengthened but management tempered aggressive prepayment of the term loan, muting deleveraging upside. The print is positive but much of it was priced in.

Revenue landed essentially in the modeled ~$2.0M range and cash/runway looked clean, and crucially the feared $4M+ non‑cash stock‑comp hit did not materialize (EPS far better than the pre‑flagged GAAP expectation) — positives that should drive a constructive near‑term reaction. Offsets: prior‑auth approval remains only ~31% (still short of the >40% inflection investors want) and management flags higher H2 burn for hiring, tempering upside.

Commercial Foodservice organic growth meaningfully beat and management provided the first standalone FY26 guide in line with the recast, which relieves the biggest uncertainty; partially offset by incremental H2 inflationary pressure and margin drag from the ice & beverage ramp. Net = modestly positive relative to the note's base case.

Consolidated revenue meaningfully missed the pre-release consensus (~$34M vs $24.3M) and management declined to reinstate guidance, which will weigh on sentiment for a stock that had run up; offsetting this, orders, backlog (book-to-bill 1.5x) and cash/availability surprised to the upside, showing underlying demand strength.

Underlying operating performance was essentially in line with the preview once you strip the non‑cash one-offs, and staking yield was strong, but the mark-to-market gain and revenue were slightly below the analyst's priors and management gave no clear buyback/return-of-capital commitment — a mixed print that is modestly positive vs. consensus but not a clear catalyst.

Clear upside across the income statement and cash: revenue and adjusted EBITDA materially beat the pre-release base case, cash ended well above the modeled range, and management pushed a larger-than-expected 45Z monetization cadence plus a >$40M customer-funded expansion. The stock’s elevated run-up tempers some upside, but the print is unambiguously better than the note’s base/bear cases.

Audience Modeling (IntentKey) growth materially beat the low bar and management provided an explicit breakeven roadmap, which offers relief for a beaten-down stock; those positives offset a slight revenue/EPS miss, sharp gross-margin compression and one-time charges.

Release largely matched the preview (cash from the $100M raise on the balance sheet and timing reiterations) but added two modestly positive, non-anticipated items — runway explicitly extended into 2H 2028, expanded endometriosis plans funded, and new modeling showing >90% receptor occupancy — so a mildly positive market reaction is likely despite the name being richly priced.

Massive revenue and margin misses plus a dramatic cut to FY26 guidance (midpoint down ~46% vs prior guide) on weaker antimony prices — the stock went into the print priced-for-perfection, so the guide reset is a clear bearish catalyst despite stronger liquidity and a Larvotto mark-to-market gain.

Operational beats were clear (same-location NOI +12%, RevPAS ~$225, utilization and volumes accelerated) while management simply reaffirmed prior guidance; upside is therefore real but constrained because the stock is deal-priced and the take‑private IOI expires tomorrow, so the decisive move awaits the Special Committee.

Quarter was essentially the base case (guidance reiterated) but contained multiple unanticipated positives — revenue beat, stronger-than-expected product gross margins (raised FY margin guide), a partner moving into commercial contract negotiations, and a slightly larger financing/pro-forma cash runway — creating a relief-driven, modestly positive read.

Modest revenue beat plus raises to FY revenue, ARR and EBITDA guidance are constructive and weren’t fully baked in; however the ending ARR ($132.7M) sits just below the note’s critical ~$133M threshold and reported gross margin is weaker than the street wanted, leaving a mixed read for the stock.

Modest revenue beat masked by clear deterioration in the underlying business: adjusted EBITDA materially missed expectations and core Managed IT growth decelerated to ~8%; margin compression from a loss on a large order and procurement mix makes the print negative despite the top-line beat.

Q2 was essentially in-line with guidance on revenue and delivered improving margins and a small positive adj. EBITDA; management raised FY adj. EBITDA to $2–3M but the lift is materially driven by a >$2M AIPA tariff refund (one-time). Early hit of the proprietary-brand target and an executed buyback are genuine positives, but underlying ops excluding one-offs are broadly inline with the preview.

Headline EPS/massive net loss was driven by the pre-announced $200M Tanabe royalty buyout (anticipated in the preview), while the call delivered the more important fundamentals the note flagged: cash slightly above expectations with runway 'into 2028' reaffirmed, disciplined G&A (~$24.7M) and favorable clinical/competitive read-through vs. baxdrostat — a modestly positive, relief-driven outcome.

Modest revenue beat on the headline (inline vs consensus) but a clear upside in underlying RNS growth (21.3%), a small upward tweak to FY revenue and margin/adj. EBITDA guidance, plus constructive SIR timing commentary — offset by weaker cash and a still-challenging H2 ramp requirement. Net: modestly positive relief.

Management raised FY26 revenue and year-end cash guidance, reported stronger-than-expected Q2 revenue and materially higher gross margins, and backlog jumped to ~$2B — all positives that were not fully priced in; an EPS/adjusted EBITDA miss tempers the strength but the guidance lift and balance-sheet improvement should drive a strong next-day reaction, amplified by the short-interest setup.

Quarter showed stronger-than-expected revenue/EBITDA and record conversion/retention, and management guided FY27 well above Street (EPS midpoint ~6.14 vs $5.86 consensus) while explicitly normalizing the tax rate to ~23%. The stock is nevertheless stretched into the print and capital-return upside was smaller than some hoped (buyback size not re‑upped to the bull-case expectation), tempering the reaction.

Headline beat was driven largely by unexpected ex‑US license/milestone cash and a materially lower SG&A run‑rate; underlying product revenue/scripts missed the analyst's 30k+ script hurdle, but July MoM prescription acceleration and strong refill metrics provide a credible path to recovery. Net effect: positive but tempered by one‑time nature of the revenue and no formal spend ceiling.

Record revenue and a materially better underlying adjusted EBITDA (ex-refund) surprised to the upside, plus strong subscription and international performance; however the sizable FY EBITDA raise and GM lift are driven by a one-time ~$4M tariff refund, muting sustainable upside.

Revenue came in materially below the preview/consensus and management flagged near-term same-store softness, which outweighs the beat in adjusted EBITDA, improved SG&A and stronger liquidity/progress on refinancing — a net negative for a stock trading on the turnaround narrative.

Mixed print: adj. EBITDA beat the derived Street range but was aided materially by tariff refunds and recent acquisitions, while revenue and base-business volumes disappointed and the Green Giant Canada close slipped to Q3; guidance was merely reaffirmed. Overall the underlying story is inline-to-slightly negative for the deleveraging thesis.

Q2 beat modestly on shipment of the delayed FWA order, stronger-than-expected gross margin and an unexpected seven-figure defense revenue stream plus ATM proceeds that lifted cash; however management refused to give Q3 guidance and margin was helped by sales of previously written-down inventory (one-time), leaving uncertainty and dilution risk.

Q2 revenue missed consensus by ~12.7%, but management reaffirmed FY26 guidance and cash (+$209.5M) and active buybacks provide a valuation floor; mixed signals (missed quarter vs. supportive cash/guidance) point to a modestly negative next-day reaction.

The quarter missed the note's revenue/bookings expectations materially, but management explicitly reaffirmed the ~$11M deferred-revenue recognition in Q3 and cash improved; given the stock ran up into the print (priced for perfection), the misses dominate and imply a negative near-term reaction.

Q2 revenue and gross margin materially exceeded the preview model (2.1M vs ~1.8M; margin ~75% vs expected ~60%), net loss narrowed, and management disclosed additional grant/program detail — all clear positives. That said the 100% growth target was merely reaffirmed (no quant H2 bridge) and the stock had run up into the print, so upside should be substantial but not flawless.

Revenue was roughly in line with the preview but slightly below consensus, while a much stronger-than-expected margin and aggressive Q3/Q4 revenue guide (new guidance initiated) signal the $3.2M backlog converting into near-term sales; however, persistent high opex, elevated cash burn and dilution/listing overhang limit upside.

Q2 revenue missed consensus by ~9.6% and the updated quarterly cadence implies FY26 below the company’s prior “>$40M” framing, but demand indicators (sharp catheter revenue growth, first GenesisX order, Synchrony contribution) reduce the hit; mixed signals leave a modestly negative near-term reaction.

Revenue beat was largely pre-baked and margins improved sequentially, but the balance sheet and working-capital build remain problematics (large inventory, substantial 1H burn and continued going-concern language) and management gave no firm sustained-breakeven timeline — a mixed print with limited upside.

Cash plunged to ~$5.6M (well below the ~9.5–10M the note flagged as the financing hinge) and management issued a going-concern warning; the new business-combination LOI that would leave existing shareholders with ~5–10% is effectively dilutive and materially negative. A Yorkville principal paydown and some burn improvement are positives but do not offset the acute liquidity/ownership risks.

Clear upside across revenue, bookings, and a materially higher-than-expected adjusted EBITDA margin plus a raise that pushes FY midpoint above $1.03B — all three key gates passed. The stock was richly positioned into the print, so upside should be strong but not fully runaway.

Quarter printed broadly in line with the pre-release yardstick but with modest upside in EBITDA/EPS and a traffic-led +9% comp; crucially management reiterated FY guidance and framed the cyclospora impact as contained with sequential recovery — a relief-driven outcome but upside limited by H2 margin headwinds.

EBITDA guidance was raised and management showed clear software pricing and installed-base traction (and initiated a strategic review of the casino business), but revenue printed essentially inline (with a $1M tariff adjustment) and recurring revenue growth disappointed versus the higher pre-call hopes; the stock entered the print priced-for-perfection.

Managed-services bookings materially missed the preview/whisper (down 19% to $4.5M versus the expected ~ $7M+ range), and MS revenue plunged 36% YoY, undermining the H2 return-to-growth story; cash remains a floor but not enough to offset the bookings-driven reset.

Q delivered several unanticipated program positives (100% 12‑month responder rate, ASPIRE completed, PPQ still on track with Catalent commercial supply) and a cash print ($455M) that extends runway beyond the note's base case, but the stock is priced for perfection and an SAE was disclosed; overall positive but upside is tempered by positioning.

Cash came in materially stronger than the note feared ($14M) and the Avenue tranche/loan terms provide runway, removing near-term dilution risk; offset by a sizable revenue miss versus consensus and meaningful margin contraction plus minimal commercial staffing and no quantified LOIs/POs. Net = modestly positive relief but not a validation of the commercial case.

Quarter was roughly in-line with company guidance but below Street revenue/OIBDA expectations; the surprise was the large Captivate acquisition financed with $275M of debt, plus pausing the dividend/buybacks and no forward guide — these balance-sheet and capital-return hits should drive a negative reaction despite strong local revenue and attendance.

Q1 guidance (mid $1.25B / EPS midpoint ~$4.20) materially exceeds the pre-release derived consensus and the company signaled durable margin expansion and faster OCS/pump-laser ramps; the large GAAP one-time charge is non-cash and does not change the positive underlying beat.

Revenue missed consensus by ~13% and was down sequentially (negative for a name that needs H2 ramp), but management reaffirmed FY26 guide and reported better-than-expected 22.6% gross margin plus strong, multi-year drone order visibility and a clear production ramp — mixed overall, leaning slightly negative given the high sensitivity to execution.

Revenue and EPS came in meaningfully better than the note's model (beat on both), and VigilAigent ARR / a large Texas contract were confirmed, but cash was far worse than expected ($0.2M) and management pushed cash-flow positivity into 2027, making near-term dilution highly likely.

Pro forma liquidity (~$300M) and the post-redemption share count (~165–167M) largely matched the preview (removing a major tail risk), and management reported regulatory progress (draft PNT NPRM in interagency review) plus commercial partnerships; however, GAAP was hurt by a ~$32M noncash derivative/warrant loss and the lower 900 MHz band was omitted from the FCC's final direct-to-device NPRM — on a stock that ran up into the print, those negatives should produce a modestly negative near-term reaction.

Mixed print — material Q2 revenue and EPS misses and a lower quarter-end cash balance weigh negative, but the board executed a meaningful $3.2M buyback and the company signed a major device licensee and new exhibitor partnerships; overall the market reaction should be modestly positive/neutral given the cash-heavy valuation and remaining execution risks.

Management reiterated the critical 'late 2026' topline timing and cash came in a bit stronger (~$110M), but EPS/margin missed the preview and management declined to disclose powering details, leaving study interpretability and financing risk unresolved — a muted to slightly-negative reaction is likely.

Big revenue miss vs consensus (no Saudi $1.475M recognition) but materially better cash and much-lower R&D run-rate plus confirmed sBLA timetable — commercial execution remains the key open risk, while financing runway concern is alleviated.

The print largely confirmed the pre-announced regulatory progress (resubmission on track for Q3, 6-month base-case review) and reaffirmed FY guidance while delivering a material revenue beat and a surprisingly narrower adj. EBITDA loss; a one-off $11.7M debt extinguishment widened GAAP loss but does not change the underlying story.

Q2 revenue missed the $6.0M bar and Q3 guide was flat at $5.5M with two key opportunities pushed to 2027 (including the Intel 18A slip), which lowers the FY consensus; partially offset by much stronger gross margins and a large ATM that boosted cash and de-risked near-term liquidity.

Most quarter-level good news (revenue, margin, $60B orders) was pre-announced and largely priced in; the company nevertheless initiated an above-whisper FY27 revenue guide and materially repaired the balance sheet, but Q1 margin guidance is much lower than Q4’s mid‑teens, leaving a mixed take and a modestly positive re-rating.

Revenue came in exactly in line with the model, but adjusted gross margin and adjusted EBITDA were worse than expected and cash exited lighter than modeled; that said, a $12.5M post-quarter strategic follow-on materially eases immediate financing risk, leaving a modestly positive relief reaction.

Big top-line and EPS beat, but management says the Q2 strength was driven by Chiesi inventory management (one-off timing) and no fresh FY guidance/affirmation or PRX‑119 disclosure was provided; cash came in below the preferred threshold — net effect is a moderately positive, muted reaction.

Cash runway was reaffirmed through the 2029 PERFORMA readout (removing the main dilution fear) and clinical updates were largely as-expected; incremental positives (early FIB‑4 improvement and confirmed RESTORE enrollment/analysis plan) give modest upside, but most of the print was already priced in.

A clean quarter (revenue and EPS beats, record ARR) plus a FY raise and a GS‑advised T&L strategic review are material positives; offset only modestly by a Field Systems ARR guide cut. Net is a meaningfully positive, but not unambiguously blown‑out, outcome.

Commercial results were strong (product sales and margins beat/held up) but the print included a slight EPS miss and management merely reiterated an "at least $1B by 2027" target that sits below Street 2027 consensus, and the stock arrived priced for perfection with the legal overhang unresolved — a mixed-but-muted outcome.

Q2 was largely inline on revenue but materially better on margin and EPS, and management raised AOI/narrowed the FY range — a rare guidance-positive outcome — offset by pronounced traffic weakness, a sizable inventory build and a trimmed comp top end; mixed but skewed positive.

Management raised FY adj. EPS and materially lifted adj. gross-margin guidance and announced a $400M ASR tied to the Lee close — a clear positive vs the base case — offset by flat Wrangler U.S. wholesale and a $25M reinvestment drag that mutes the upside.

Revenue materially missed the ~$7M consensus and management cut FY26 guide to $20–23M (midpoint well below prior midpoint), while gross margin and adjusted EBITDA deteriorated; positives (larger-than-expected cash post-offering and follow-on orders) provide some cushion but do not offset the guide cut.

Q4 revenue and AOI materially beat the pre-release base case (revs $196.3M; AOI swung to $18.6M), management quantified a $47M cash arena license fee run-rate and the Christmas Spectacular produced a much larger revenue haul than expected — but there's no explicit FY27 financial guide or buyback upsized and the stock was already richly valued, so upside is positive but not extreme.

Headline numbers were largely as previewed (GAAP revenue ~ $2M; a one-time ~$11M license gain produced the noisy EPS outcome). The call delivered helpful color — a $1.40/MHz-POP benchmark, stronger cash ($116M) and an active pipeline — but no material newly signed large 10 MHz deals, so the print confirms progress without delivering the catalyst the market was paying for.

Q4 EPS was inline and comps/traffic were modestly better, but the decisive outcome is a materially higher FY27 guide (midpoint ~$13.00) and commentary that July/August accelerated — a clear beats-the-bar on the forward story despite a slight restaurant-margin miss in the quarter.

Revenue modestly beat the analyst build and management executed on buybacks and new contracts, but EPS and quarter EBITDA missed the note's base estimate and management guided SLS margins lower than the note anticipated — a mixed print that leans negative.

Revenue, adj. EBITDA (ex‑charter), operating cash flow and a very large 2027 revenue target were materially better than the thin consensus, but a sizeable EPS miss driven by a $2.9M vessel charter drag and a large run-up into the print limit upside until the charter is clearly one‑time.

Q4 was broadly inline (adj. EPS roughly in line, adj. EBITDA at the top of the implied range) while FY27 adj. EBITDA guidance (midpoint $2.175B) modestly exceeds the Street/preview bridge — validating the acceleration story but not overwhelmingly so given the stock's premium multiple.

Underlying results materially missed the pre-release yardstick: adj. EPS and adj. EBITDA collapsed and gross margin dipped below the analyst's base-case, while GAAP EPS was artificially bolstered by a one-time bargain-purchase gain. Offsetting positives — a large, unexpected backlog build, stronger cash from operations, and tuck-in aerospace acquisitions — are real but likely viewed as longer‑lead benefits, so the market should punish the near-term margin/earnings miss.

Most of the call confirmed the note's base case: C‑BEYOND win already known, C‑FORWARD timing set (topline early Q1'27) and an NDA anticipated in Q2'27 (clarity reduces uncertainty), cash came in slightly ahead of the preview and runway is through 2027; downside risks (no partner, intent to self-commercialize) leave the print mixed-to-neutral. No one‑time items drove the positives.

The print removes the Nasdaq delisting overhang: Q2 equity of $2.7M and $5.4M cash (including ~$4.9M ATM proceeds) materially exceed the $2.5M threshold and extend runway into 2027; regulatory commentary from PMDA/FDA adds optionality. Enrollment remains slow and operational progress is modest, but the balance-sheet relief dominates near-term market reaction.

Big Q2 revenue beat and a material FY26 revenue raise to ~$15M (50% above prior guide) and stronger-than-expected quarter-end cash drive a positive after-hours reaction; the surprise delay of 200 kW commercialization into 2027 tempers upside and leaves further re-pricing contingent on Wednesday’s call.

Revenue came in below the $21.23M consensus (~$19.3M) while consolidated adjusted EBITDA came in materially higher — but that beat was materially driven by non-recurring stock-for-service deals and liability eliminations; management's aggressive buybacks and aspirational multi-year revenue targets provide narrative positives but do not erase the credibility/questions around sustainability.

Revenue ($16.1M) missed the pre-release consensus (~$18M / buy-side bar ~$17M) and management provided no quantified AI/licensing disclosure or FY27 guide update — the primary catalyst — while adjusted EBITDA and contribution margin outperformed expectations and the balance sheet is clean. Mixed read but skewed negative given the absent AI monetization details.

Cisco beat the quarter modestly but, more importantly, materially raised FY27 revenue and EPS guidance and lifted the FY27 AI revenue target — a clear upside surprise versus the Street that should drive a strong positive reaction despite the stock's rich positioning.

Operational quarter came in ahead of the pre-release base case — Emrosi revenue, scripts, ASP and adjusted EBITDA all materially stronger — but management again provided no FY guidance, leaving the key consensus-gap unresolved and limiting upside.

Revenue, EBITDA, gross margin and adj. EPS all beat the pre-release yardstick and management raised FY comp/net sales/EBITDA and EPS ranges; the guide lift materially reduces the bear-case H2 risk. A near-term Q3 cyclospora headwind tempers the upside but does not offset the otherwise clear beat-and-raise.

Quarter hit the top of guidance and EPS materially outperformed consensus, while management raised Q1 revenue materially above the street and quantified LTAs/backlog — clear fundamental beats. That said, an elevated capex print and the stock's rich entry price temper upside, so expect a strong but not runaway reaction.

Q2 showed slightly stronger-than-modeled revenue and a better-than-expected cash balance, enrollment progress is close to the run-rate needed to hit year-end targets, and no dilutive financing was announced — a modestly constructive print against a low bar.

Management reaffirmed double-digit SaaS growth (a relief vs the note's skepticism) but the quarter showed weaker profitability, higher opex and a still-modest SaaS uptick; beaten-down positioning and cash near $1.7M limit downside while capping upside until guide is evidenced by stronger SaaS execution.

Topline timing slipped from August to mid-September and cash ($10.1M) came in below the analyst's $11.0–11.5M runway expectation; quarter showed wider loss and lower revenue — management's upbeat BLA/partnership framing is insufficient to offset the financing/timing shortfall.

Revenue was already pre-announced and came in inline, but EPS missed materially and opex/cash metrics were worse-than-hope (opex up to $13.8M, cash only $8.2M), leaving dilution/going-concern risk as the dominant takeaway.

Modest upside to core and total revenue plus clear buyback execution and a visible Genentech partnership contrast with a maintained FY guide, only-moderately better margins, and slightly higher-than-expected opex — a modestly positive, largely priced-in print.

KOMZIFTI delivered solid product revenue (9.1M) with 115 new starts and >250 prescriptions, management explicitly denied inventory/one-off effects, payor coverage improved and KOMET-007 clinical data were very strong — all of which materially exceed the pre-print base case despite guidance being merely reiterated.

Revenue and gross margin modestly beat the preview (revenue $33.5M vs base $32M; margin 17% vs 16.2%) and backlog grew meaningfully, but EPS slightly missed and the print revealed material working-capital-driven cash burn and higher revolver usage — on a stock that had run up, this mix should produce a muted-to-negative near-term reaction.

A decisive launch acceleration: Q2 net sales of $28.5M materially exceed the pre-release base-case ($15.5M), account count and cash flow are much stronger than feared, and management moved up the timing to mid‑2027 for company-wide cash‑flow positivity. The non‑cash derivative gain clouds the GAAP headline but adjusted results and recurring revenue metrics are unambiguously better.

Late-cycle review completed and the Oct 30 PDUFA date was reaffirmed with only one inspection observation addressed (regulatory relief), opex and net loss came in meaningfully better than modeled, but EPS strength was materially driven by a $9M non-cash warrant fair-value gain and runway is only extended into late Q1 2027 (shorter than the note's mid-2027 hope).

The stock had re-rated into the Hanford IDIQ (priced in ahead of the print). The quarter missed revenue and EPS materially versus the pre-release anchors and retained a going-concern qualification; cash and backlog were positives but insufficient to offset the miss — likely a sell-the-news outcome.

Revenue beat consensus modestly and operating cash burn roughly halved to ~$3.7M with cash/runway intact and management reaffirming 'cash flow positive exiting 2026' — these reliefs outweigh a tick-down in gross margin and continued Gen‑3 timing uncertainty, producing a modestly positive next‑day outlook.

Underlying adjusted EBITDA (ex one-time retention and litigation charges) looks better than the preview's bar and cash actually improved to $7.7M while the CEO is buying into >5%; however headline EBITDA and GAAP EPS were hurt by ~$0.72–0.8M of one-offs, producing a muddled print.

Management hit the one thing the market cared most about — they reaffirmed the $95–100M / $21–25M EBITDA guide — but underlying health looks worse: NRR collapsed to 90%, average customer metrics fell and the CFO succession plus severance costs raise execution risk; upsides (gross-margin raise, DSP go-live, faster debt paydown) blunt but do not offset the negatives.

Concrete operational progress (75% enrolled, all sites activated) plus supportive regulatory/commercial signals (KDIGO mention, larger market estimate, good dosing/safety data) with cash roughly as expected and tranches intact — a clear positive for the timing narrative that drives valuation.

Top-line and comps/traffic surprised modestly to the upside and restaurant-level margin expanded, but adjusted EBITDA missed materially due to higher marketing spend and management left FY26 guidance unchanged (still excluding the refranchising impact) — a mixed print into a stock priced for perfection.

Management accelerated site activation (~100 sites by year-end) and confirmed RMAT/fast-track + durable activity in ALLO-316 and an earlier-than-expected ALLO-329 update, which materially de-risks the enrollment timeline; the need for “overwhelming” efficacy to hit the interim EFS read tempers upside. No runway/opex hit was disclosed, so the print is net-positive but not a binary re-rate.

Usio raised FY26 revenue growth to 14–16% and delivered a 24% gross margin plus a second consecutive GAAP profit ($0.01), upgrading the fundamental story; however the stock went into the print rich, so upside is meaningful but somewhat muted.

Operational beat (EBITDA +10%) and stronger generation/PPA revenue contrasted with a revenue miss and no refinancing progress — going-concern remains — so equity (a refinancing call option) is likely to trade down despite the quarter.

Revenue came in below the pre-release yardstick and EPS materially missed, driven in part by large retooling / one-time margin hits; those negatives are offset by clear commercial progress (retailer ~90% complete, diversification, govt POC) and an explicit reaffirmation of no ATM usage, leaving a mixed print and a modestly negative near-term reaction.

Headline revenue and margin beat aided by strong Groovy Girls sell-through and large tariff-refund recognition, but the beat is largely one-time and management cut the dividend — underlying results (ex-refunds) missed the note's model, so the print should be viewed negatively overall.

Results matched the preview: a small revenue miss driven by higher grant (low-margin) revenue, a deeper EPS miss, and a going-concern disclosure that was already public and already drove most of the stock move; the remaining call risk centers on financing/dilution and is skewed negative but largely priced in.

Material upside to the licensing line, revenue, margins and adj. EBITDA plus a raise to FY guidance clear the credibility bar the market cared about; modestly conservative H2 EBITDA guidance and the low quarter-end cash balance are the lone offsets. Overall this should trigger a strong relief rally from a beaten-down starting point.

Continuing-ops results slightly beat the analyst model (revenue and margin) but the critical forward-looking metrics — orders and backlog — missed and a booked system order is now at bankruptcy risk; the headline profit is one-time from the SDC sale and should not prop up the stock. No capital-allocation surprise was delivered.

Revenue and buy-side core growth came in roughly as our base case, but liquidity (cash down to $0.5M) and an ongoing covenant waiver request leave the capital-structure binary unresolved — a net negative for the equity.

Revenue, margin and cash were pre-released and met expectations; the headline GAAP loss was largely a one-time, noncash accounting item as anticipated, while adjusted EBITDA reaching breakeven and cash stability are positive — offset by shrinking backlog and no definitive acquisition financing/close.

Revenue and margins materially beat the pre-print working numbers, management raised FY sales and margin guidance and moved to positive FCF — a clear fundamental upgrade that also addresses liquidity; the stock had run up into the print so some of the beat was anticipated.

Marks/Treasury gains were larger than modelled and NAV/redeployment details materially reduced the key redeployment risk, but the headline profit is largely mark-driven (non‑recurring) and management did not announce any buyback/capital‑allocation action — guidance was merely reiterated.

Q2 prints beat consensus modestly and showed tangible execution (eyewear shipments, smartphone test progress, a larger Korea/drone pipeline), but the new Q3 guide (midpoint $9.5M) is below the ~$11M the Street needs to preserve FY26 consensus — a guide-driven disappointment outweighing the operational positives. Expect a weak to neutral stock reaction.

Large revenue miss (Q2 -17% vs model -6.8%) and 17% order decline outweigh the margin/EBITDA beat and new financing; stock was priced-for-perfection so the topline disappointment should drive a negative reaction.

Q2 materially beat revenue/eps and management raised FY revenue and EPS guidance while improving gross-margin guidance and showing stronger backlog conversion and book-to-bill; with the stock beaten down into the print, this should be viewed positively.

Q3 delivered better-than-expected operating EPS and a sizable adj. EBITDA beat and material debt paydown, but same-store sales slightly missed management's 'approaching flat' bar and management narrowed/lowered FY EBITDA and RLM guidance — a disappointment for a stock that ran up into the print.

Q2 was roughly inline to slightly light on revenue and cash declined, but management delivered materially better-than-expected combined Q3 guidance (revenue and adj. EBITDA) tied to a full quarter of the Arcania acquisition; mixed Q2 cash flow and convertible/dilution overhang limit upside.

Top-line and adj. EBITDA materially missed consensus and management withdrew FY guidance, confirming the restructuring/balance-sheet risk the market had been trading; however much of that risk was already priced in, so the move should be muted unless the 10‑Q adds a going‑concern paragraph or new financing detail.

NRC timing was reaffirmed and the balance sheet is stronger than modeled, but the STS revenue stub was far smaller than the note's run-rate expectation and the company did raise ~$26M via the ATM — a clear negative. Net: mixed, with downside pressure dominating given dilution risk and absent binding commercial wins.

Most negatives were already flagged (sale of Movies, ROI plan, withdrawn guidance), but the underlying adj. EBITDA collapsed to $1.3M and management reinstated guidance at a lowered midpoint with low-to-mid single-digit EBITDA margins and no near-term growth — a clear negative for the stock. The print delivers little upside catalyst (no Series C resolution) and confirms a weaker operating trajectory.

Cash/runway was reaffirmed (key floor) and payer engagement/partnerships surprised to the upside, but revenue fell well below the preview consensus, opex/burn ticked up and CE submission slipped — net outcome is mixed-to-slightly-negative for the stock.

Modest revenue beat and improved underlying cash flow/adj. EBITDA with guidance reaffirmed are positives, but the $40M equity placement (dilutive) and the stock's high pre-print positioning temper upside — net neutral-to-slightly-negative next-day reaction.

All of the material events (FDA approval, royalty financing, SP001 in‑licensing and Phase II timing) were already public and the quarter landed essentially in line; management did confirm runway into 2H‑2029 and provided SP001 Phase II details, which is modest relief for a beaten‑down stock trading below net cash.

Headline revenue and EPS beat, but results were aided by a non‑recurring $27M tariff refund; management issued the first standalone FY26 guide that is slightly below the analyst 'bogey' (~$3.0B/$620M), and flagged a $40–50M H2 OEM volume hit plus rising input‑cost headwinds. Net: mixed but modestly negative given sustainability concerns.

The print mixed: a material timeline slip (first commercial moved to Feb‑2027) and a worse Q3 FCF guide outweigh a stronger-than-expected cash position from a large ATM and debt reduction. On a stock that ran up into the print, the slip + guide hit is the dominant negative.

Revenue missed the derived street proxy (driven by near-zero battery resale), but the quarter delivered better-than-feared operating metrics — $6M adj. EBITDA, record 55% non‑GAAP gross margin, OCF breakeven, stronger bookings/backlog and a cash raise — and management reaffirmed guidance (midpoint above consensus), so the print is net positive versus the bear case.

Record revenue, China demand described as end-market (no inventory) and stronger-than-expected EVO+ adoption and margins, but EPS missed consensus and management did not reinstate FY guidance — operational relief offset by continued guidance uncertainty.

Revenue modestly beat consensus and FY26 guidance was reaffirmed with a higher contracted percentage (>85%) plus a material arbitration award — clear relief vs. the bear case — but a sharp drop in non-GAAP gross margin to 38% and continued H2 concentration temper the upside.

Headline GAAP gain (>$90M) likely secures Nasdaq compliance and materially improves the balance sheet, while underlying operating results are mixed — a stronger-than-expected EBITDA and bigger cost savings offset a worse-than-expected same-station revenue decline. The print is therefore a mixed fundamental read but a net positive for the delisting/catalyst narrative.

Company reaffirmed FY guidance and reported a modest revenue beat and higher US XPOVIO sales, plus materially positive FDA written feedback supporting SVR35 as a surrogate and an on-track August sNDA — but cash remains tight (~$65M) with a September/October covenant cliff and no named financing, so upside is limited but the print is net constructive.

Q2 delivered essentially what the preview treated as the base case: revenue inline and gross margin improved to ~18% with full-year guidance reiterated. Offsetting modest weakness in adj. EBITDA, the beat-to-bear risks were removed by strong operating cash flow, a higher cash balance and an explicit no-capital-raise message, so the print should be modestly positive.

Tapestry beat the quarter and — most importantly — issued FY27 guidance ($7.80–7.90 midpoint $7.85) meaningfully above street/Amplify expectations, alongside margin expansion, a bigger buyback and a dividend raise; however the stock was priced for perfection so upside should be positive but somewhat muted.

Revenue came in below the consensus/base-case (miss) but management reaffirmed CY2026 and CY2027 guidance, pushed Gen‑2 timing toward Q4 (H2) and delivered better-than-expected cash and gross-margin — a relief print for a beaten-down stock rather than a re-rating catalyst.

Sharp revenue miss and worsening adjusted EBITDA, plus cash ($6.1M) below the pre-call base case, outweigh a headline gross-loss improvement that was largely driven by a one-time tax recovery; financing/dilution risk remains primary.

Revenue and EPS beat the pre-print build, management reported July volumes tracking to the mid/upper guidance range and signed supply deals with all top 5 dialysis providers, and they raised adj. EBITDA guidance — a relief print versus the feared collapse. Results are partly flattered by a one-time $4.2M insurance reimbursement that boosts G&A (tempering quality).

Modest revenue beat and a material commercial win (Concert LBM adoption + higher recognized % vs. Q1) are positives, but no news on the critical Aug‑22 waiver, VA revenue is delayed to Oct 1, cash is lower than the preview's pro‑forma expectation and adjudicated allowable per test drifted down — a mixed print with a slight negative tilt given the looming waiver risk.

Revenue slightly missed consensus due to low-yield and out-of-spec manufacturing batches that prevented recognition of several treatments, and management's decision to abandon biopsy-based forward indicators materially reduces visibility — on a stock priced for perfection that combination should produce a negative reaction despite positives (7th QTC, NTAP, improving yields).

Quarter materially beat the preview/consensus on revenue, recurring revenue, procedures, margin (even excluding a $1.1M tariff refund) and produced a surprise positive adjusted EBITDA / GAAP swing; no new guidance but backlog and cash are intact, so the print is unambiguously positive versus the base and bear cases.

Results largely confirmed the Aug 6 pre-announcement: cash (~$8.8M) avoids the immediate bear trigger, first patient dosed and run-in anecdotes reiterated, and named‑patient program launched (revenue deferred to Q3). No fresh financing or materially better clinical readout arrived, so the print is largely priced in and should produce a muted reaction.

Revenue was inline but EPS materially beat and management raised FY EPS and gross-margin guidance; however much of the Q2 margin/EPS beat was driven by an $8.2M IEEPA refund and SG&A deleverage plus flat U.S. drinkware temper the print.

Cash and the May financing were confirmed and NDA timing is largely inline, but reported loss/EPS were slightly worse than the pre-release yardstick, R&D spend materially exceeded the note's build, and Phase‑3 FPI/CLR‑125 data timing slipped modestly — a net mildly negative print given the stock is driven by milestone-tied financing.

Revenue and backlog materially beat and FY guide was nudged up, but a much larger-than-expected adj. EBITDA loss (~$51M vs. an expected 'peak' far smaller) and higher opex on a stock that ran up into the print will likely trigger profit-taking; positives do not fully offset the profitability miss for a priced-for-perfection name.

Headline beat and—crucially—same-clinic revenue +6% and +9% ARPC resolve the note's central organic-growth overhang; EBITDA/margin are healthy. Lack of buybacks or explicit FY guide and phased timing of the $15M fee uplift cap upside near term.

Record $1.8B backlog, $1.2B Q2 bookings and a healthy cash balance (including $235M net ATM proceeds) are materially positive and the company kept FY guidance intact; these offset a slight revenue miss and a disappointing reduction in near-term backlog conversion and continued negative adjusted EBITDA.

Slight revenue/units beat and a $10M Horizon tranche unlock plus sequential EBITDA improvement are positives, but rising gross-to-net guidance, lower realized rev/unit than the yardstick, and a one-time SG&A charge leave the print mixed; stock was priced for perfection so reaction should be modestly positive.

Revenue came in essentially at the pre-release whisper (~$88M) but adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded the de facto $12M bogey and the company generated >$36M operating cash flow, repaid the revolver and sits on $35.4M cash — materially de-risking near-term covenant/liquidity concerns and warranting a strong positive reaction despite ongoing DTC softness.

WWW beat revenue and EPS modestly and materially raised FY revenue and EPS guidance (midpoint to ~$1.60), plus GM guidance and inventories improved — a clear upside vs the preview. The limited tariff relief and some brand-level DTC softness temper but do not offset the guidance-driven positive surprise.
