Modest revenue and margin beat, plus strong cash/FCF, were offset by a reiterated FY guide (no raise) and a slip in BKR9500 timing; the print removes little H2 execution risk and is likely to produce a muted-to-slightly-negative market response. Guidance reiteration dominates despite the quarter's small upside.

Gross margin materially exceeded expectations and opex fell sequentially, supporting the structural-margin story; however, the June 30 cash balance came in below the analyst bridge and there was no clear removal of going-concern language, capping upside given the warrant/financing overhang.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA printed inside the pre-announced range (largely de‑risked), auditors removed the going‑concern and the financing materially boosted cash — all positives — but gross margin missed the implied ~42% recovery and GAAP EPS was materially worse than the analyst-derived estimate, leaving a modestly positive, but not triumphant, read for the stock.

Q2 delivered higher-than-modeled revenue, a return to GAAP profitability and a materially stronger adjusted EBITDA, but management cut FY26 revenue guidance materially and reported a large operating cash outflow. Because a guidance re-base was the expected outcome and the stock was already de-rated/delisted, the print is mixed and should be received as mildly positive-to-neutral.

Company beat on organic growth, margins and EPS materially, and issued an FY27 initial guide whose midpoint (~$11.90) sits above consensus — plus very strong Engineered Solutions orders — outweighing valuation headwinds. The combination of an across-the-board operational beat and a better-than-expected initial guide drives a strongly positive reaction despite the stock trading at a premium.

The quarter was already public and largely priced in; the call supplied mixed color — product gross margin expansion and an inventory-build to shorten lead times are positives, but no named data-center orders and only modest backlog conversion guidance leave consensus unreachable and runway/dilution risk unresolved. Net effect: mild-to-moderate negative reaction despite a couple operational positives.

Revenue and EBITDA materially beat conservative consensus and, critically, management raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance well above prior ranges; PDS spread expansion, preferred-payer momentum, a California rate win and credit/interest savings reinforce the upside despite sponsor overhang and a recent run-up.

Revenue essentially inline to the pre-release bar, but management guided Q2 materially above the working bar and reported very strong data-center orders and PPS strength; however the headline EPS beat is materially assisted by one-time tariff/tax refunds and some 45X items, lowering quality.

NAV visibly beat the implied mark (to $8.25) driven by repurchases and meaningful Debbie recoveries, and management initiated foreclosure / marketing actions on Justice Grown — all of which materially reduce the bear-case tail risk; NII was essentially inline.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA materially beat the pre-release yardstick and gross margin expanded to ~80%, but cash fell to $4.7M, a going-concern remains and an ITC exclusion order impacts a meaningful subset of lamps — with the stock already at a 52-week high the net reaction should be muted/neutral.

Q4 revenue and AOI materially beat the preview/base case and management put a firm end-October spin-off completion window on the Rangers separation; however the stock was richly priced into the print so upside is substantial but not extreme.

Revenue ($0.9M) missed the modelled Q2 base and cash plunged to $2M, creating acute NASDAQ-compliance/liquidity risk; debt exchanges and a Toolkit product release are helpful but insufficient to offset the shortfall.

Revenue cleared the high end of management's guide and GAAP/adjusted EPS and gross margin materially beat the yardstick; however many of the positives (Q4 ~$30M read-through, Aydin contribution, strong organic growth ex-F‑16) were anticipated, so the market should react modestly positive rather than exuberantly.

Underlying operations beat: Q4 adj. operating margin (4.9%) and gross-margin expansion were better than the guided range, and management issued a constructive FY27 revenue guide with organic growth plus quantified Helvoet contribution. Headline EPS was a miss due to a one-time 67.8% tax item, so the print should be read as an operational beat with a non-recurring earnings hit — modestly positive next-day reaction expected.

Quarter beat the note's model on revenue, adjusted EBITDA and net income, margins expanded and cash held at ~$20.3M, plus a firmer strategic-review timeline — but the company is illiquid and historically unreactive to good news, so upside is muted.

Headline revenue and EPS were crushed by a large one-time legacy claims reassessment, but management simultaneously delivered meaningful financing relief (credit-amendment providing ~$27M cash service relief and a plan to convert surety advances into perpetual preferred) — excluding the nonrecurring adjustment the quarter looks materially better than the pre-release yardstick. The print is relief-driven but binary risk remains until financings legally close.

Pipeline and manufacturing milestones (funnel >$400M, foundry supply agreement, hyperscaler co-development) materially exceed expectations, but management pushed automotive qualification later in favor of industrial qualification — and the stock went into the print richly bid, so mixed signals likely produce a modestly negative/neutral next-day reaction.

Revenue and backlog came in at/above the note's base case (backlog strength is supportive), but headline gross margin and newly provided H2 margin guidance sit below the Investor Day/expectations (and EPS missed due to a higher share count plus a one‑time stock comp hit). Conflicting signals => muted, slightly negative next‑day reaction.

Revenue and cash came in meaningfully above the pre-print base case (strong DPS growth and cash up to $6.8M), removing some near-term liquidity fear, but adjusted EBITDA missed and management gave no concrete sale-process/advisor detail — mixed but net positive for this distressed name.

Revenue was a slight beat and digital growth materially outperformed expectations, but station operating income missed and opex rose more than modeled while cash fell after repaying the revolver. The stock ran up into the print, so mixed signals (good digital/political progress vs. margin and cash pressure) should produce a muted-to-negative near-term reaction.

Headline beat was sizable but partly driven by a $2.1M unregulated ICFA recognition; excluding that, regulated revenue and adj. EBITDA still topped street expectations and organic connections/throughput accelerated, while management reiterated regulatory progress (Santa Cruz Nov 1) — net-positive for a beaten-down stock. D&A remains elevated and one divisional rate recovery was delayed, limiting the upside.

The quarter largely matched the post-print picture (revenues down, EPS modestly up) and there was no guidance; the upside was driven by one-time investment gains and cost cuts, while new call details (notably a sharp rise in 90+ day mortgage delinquencies, deliberate inventory build in land/residential that suppresses current income, and weaker cemetery operating results) raise near-term risk — most of this was already signposted so the stock reaction should be only modestly negative.

Management delivered the two items the market wanted most: a pro forma financing and an explicit runway statement (cash sufficient for ≥12 months), plus lower-than-expected opex and a dated timeline for Cohort 3 completion/data analysis — all of which relieve the biggest near-term risks. With the company beaten down and the financing already announced, this is a clear relief-driven positive.

Revenue roughly met the pre-print base case and Bluebird showed the expected contribution, and Oasis distributor demand surprised to the upside; however materially worse gross margin and a still-substantial adj. EBITDA loss plus low cash leave limited upside. Given the stock is beaten down, the print is relief-but-not-transformational.

Mixed print: revenue roughly in line with the model and cash modestly improved, management guided to cash-neutral FY27 and product recognition (Gartner #1) — but new ARR (~$370k) and adjusted EBITDA remained well below the pre-release base, so the release is cautiously constructive but not unambiguously positive.

Revenue was inline with guidance but adjusted EBITDA came in meaningfully ahead and management raised FY EBITDA/EPS and reiterated a >$15M exit run-rate while litigation expense is falling and cash flow is strong; however ARR add and enterprise growth fell short of the higher bar the market wanted, producing a mixed but net-positive print.

Q4 revenue guide ($10.25B) meaningfully exceeds consensus and the $10B whisper and management materially upgraded semi/advanced-packaging growth — a clear positive; however the stock came in priced for perfection and gross-margin commentary was mixed (flat at ~50.4%), so upside is strong but not unambiguous.

Management delivered the two most market-relevant items the note flagged: a quantified, lower baseline burn (<$2.5M/qtr) and meaningful clinical/regulatory progress (510(k) pre‑submission for MI detection and stronger trial enrollment), which materially reduce near‑term financing risk. Lack of any signed, named licensing partner and a large severance accrual cap potential upside.

Big revenue shortfall versus consensus and a shortened cash runway with a delayed Latin America rice launch outweigh positives (Interoc expansion, regulatory wins and cost cuts), and the stock was priced for perfection going in.

Material upside to revenue and EPS plus a sizable FY26 guide raise (>$145M vs prior >$120M and consensus ~$121M), with margins expanding and Hemangiol transitioning far faster than expected — a clear positive surprise that should drive an outsized re-rating despite richly-valued positioning.

No concurrent equity raise and cash (~$238M) roughly met expectations, which avoids the worst-case bear outcome; however EPS missed materially and management is pausing commercial readiness and withdrawing the injunction vs. Nippon Shinyaku, capping upside.

Management reaffirmed a late‑Q3 launch and disclosed a $30k/month WAC (big positive for the TAM/forecast) and showed favorable tolerability metrics and strong commercial build (88 reps, favorable gross‑to‑net), but GAAP EPS materially missed and SG&A came in above modeled range, leaving a mixed but net positive read.

Quarter delivered materially lower opex and a markedly smaller dollar net loss than modeled, and cash landed at the top of the pre-release range — all positives — but management gave no financing resolution and signaled pursuit of equity/debt, while the standstill expires the next day, leaving significant dilution/overhang risk.

Revenue materially beat consensus and adj. EBITDA returned to positive, management reaffirmed FY27 guide and disclosed larger-than-expected cost cuts and tech/CTV product traction; however direct operating margin compressed sharply and net loss/EPS widened while liquidity remains tight, leaving a mixed but modestly positive read for the stock.

Slight revenue/EPS beat, meaningful deleveraging and operational progress (out-of-stock improvement, shelf-life approvals, Amazon run-rate holding) but management did not reinstate guidance — stock trades on guidance, so the upside is capped despite constructive underlying read; thin float leaves moves amplified.

Q3 results largely matched the pre-announced/expected metrics (revenue, margins, adj. EBITDA), while the call delivered several constructive datapoints — sizable post-quarter Puerto Rico collections, stronger software bookings, and backlog growth — that materially reduce the downside tail; cash remains below the $4M covenant but was better than the worst-case feared. With guidance reaffirmed but no explicit FQ4 dollar range, the market should react modestly positive.

Q2 came in ahead of consensus (5.9M vs $5.67M) with strong adj. EBITDA and cash, but management warned FY2026 revenue could be slightly below FY25 due to a large customer evaluating multi-vendor options — the negative FY framing outweighs the quarter beat. Net: mixed quarter, guidance cut dominates near-term reaction.

Quarter largely tracked the preview (Q2 product revenue effectively nil, ~$0.2M services/royalty revenue, improved loss), but the balance-sheet picture was weaker than hoped (cash down to ~$12.6M, working-cap deficit) and the Nasdaq/listing compliance question was not resolved — offset modestly by trial progress and new nondilutive funding.

Severe operational miss (Q2 revenue far below the pre-release operating estimate and a reported gross loss) undercuts the ‘inflection’ narrative, but the balance-sheet de-risking (full repayment of the $20M facility, ~ $60M cash, Board authorization to sell remaining BTC and no ATM dilution) materially reduces financing risk — mixed signals favor a slightly negative near-term reaction.

The print largely tracked the preview's base case (thin fee flow) but delivered two constructive narrative items (PatentVest to be externally funded so MDB sheds development costs; multiple LOIs for the clearing-platform deal targeting close next quarter) that offset negatives (Paulex IPO pushed to Q4, eXoZymes' weak financing and reduced cadence for new company launches). Given the stock's deep discount and that most outcomes were anticipated, the net market reaction should be modestly positive but muted.

Revenue and gross margin came in meaningfully below the note's base case and ending cash ($13.1M) was materially below modeled runway levels, raising near-term liquidity risk despite the already-known sale-leaseback and cost cuts; recurring revenue mix and CAC improvement are minor positives.

Quarter essentially confirmed the July pre-announcement (revenue, margin, adj. EBITDA, and cash) with only minor upside; the binary refinancing/going-concern outcome remains unresolved, so no re-rating catalyst was delivered. One‑time lease remeasurement helped GAAP operating income but did not alter the underlying operating story.

QSI delivered slightly better-than-consensus revenue and improved cash/runway via cost cuts, but the decisive negative was management's Proteus launch slip into Q2 2027 (early access delayed) — that timing miss outweighs the operational positives for a story whose value hinges on on-time launch.

Q2 revenue materially missed the company guide/market consensus, but a materially stronger cash balance (>$2.8M), gross margin above 80%, two imminent customer launches and a constructive Q3 revenue guide meaningfully reduce near-term financing risk — netting to a modestly positive reaction but tempered by the credibility hit from missing the firm's $5.2M guide and an upcoming opex increase.

Q2 came in modestly above consensus with clear commercial traction (market-share and prescriber gains) and an explicit H2 cash SG&A/R&D target that signals meaningful cost cuts and runway management; offset by depressed gross margin, a lower-than-expected cash balance, and a delay of the CSU Phase 2b interim to Q1 2027. Net = better-than-feared operational demand + credible cost discipline, so a positive near-term reaction is likely given the stock's beaten-down positioning and heavy short interest.

Material revenue miss and a ~9.5% cut to FY guide (midpoint) with EBITDA-margin guidance slashed to 8–9% plus removal of Puerto Rico and SafePointe timing — all delivered into a stock that rallied into the print. Liquidity and execution admissions amplify downside.

Revenue materially missed consensus (Q2 $2.3M vs ~$4.6–5.0M est.) and EPS was crushed by a $5.7M valuation allowance, but management guided to 20+ units in Q3/Q4 and disclosed 8 finance-delayed units that will flow into Q3 — so the print is a serious near-term negative with some relief for H2.

The quarter showed clear operational progress (YoY revenue and margin expansion, training ramp, FDA clearance, record July case values) but missed revenue and EPS consensus and provided no resolution on the September convertible-note maturity — the capital-structure overhang dominates. Given the run-up into the print and the unresolved note, the market is likely to react negatively.

Revenue materially beat the house estimate (9.1M vs $8.3M) and backlog/grant commentary/reduced debt were tangible positives, but Stadco remains unprofitable and cash weakened; management only reiterated guidance, so the print is modestly positive but not a clear re-rate trigger for a stock that was priced optimistically.

Material revenue miss (Q2 ~$1.1M vs $1.502M consensus) and disappointing engineering-services ($0.2M) with higher burn and a lower cash balance should pressure the stock; operational positives (Collins moved to initial production, Amazon/AI data-center interest) are encouraging but largely qualitative and insufficient to offset the headline misses.

Revenue and EPS materially beat the pre-release anchors (Q2 revenue $5.8M vs the ~$4.0M derived estimate; EPS -$0.02 vs -$0.10), and bookings ticked up — but gross margin compressed and cash declined after the Orlando purchase and backlog edged slightly lower, with no forward numerical guidance. Net: a relief rally is likely but offset by balance-sheet and margin concerns.

Q2 revenue and unit deliveries cratered well below the preview anchor and management cut FY26 guidance — dominant negatives — while a stronger-than-expected cash balance and a healthy H1 gross margin provide limited relief.

Revenue and adj. EBITDA came in below the pre-release yardstick, but the unexpected six-month CWMS 2.5 bridge (and firmness around the carrier SaaS go‑live) materially reduces the protest tail risk. Lack of formal FY guidance and a CRO retirement are offsetting negatives, leaving a modestly negative near-term read.

Management refused to reaffirm the critical $50M FY2026 target (guidance withdrawn), which overwhelms a revenue print that was roughly inline with consensus and mixed operational detail (LOI/order converts and Series A cash are positives, but margin fell sequentially and the loss widened). Net negative on balance.

Adj. EBITDA turned positive (the buy‑side bar) and management reaffirmed $18–22M guidance, which is relief for a beaten‑down stock; revenue missed and bad‑debt expense rose, leaving a mixed but overall modestly positive read.

Operational print strong (revenue/ARR/NRR materially better than the thin consensus and cash came in well above our estimate), but the company declined to announce a reverse-split ratio/date and appears to accept a lower gross-margin target (>70% vs prior ~80%) — the missing split is the dominant market risk.

The company secured meaningful non-dilutive capital (Avenue facility + SimpliDerm proceeds) and explicitly extended runway to 2028, removing the biggest overhang and outweighing a modest revenue miss and higher R&D-driven EBITDA loss; some of the cash improvement is driven by one-time sale/financing.

The headline non-cash charge (~$21.7M) landed inside the pre-announced/expected range so the main tail-risk was priced in, but revenue missed consensus and underlying operating metrics (ex-HGC) were weaker than the note hoped, leaving a mixed but not catastrophic read for the stock.

A very large revenue miss versus the ~$3.4M consensus, plus withdrawal of Accelsius targets and extension of breakeven beyond 2026 (and removal of a material PO), materially worsens the story; the modest SEPA raise and third‑party cooling benchmark are the only offsets.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA came in above the preview model and gross margin ticked up, but the company swung to a materially larger-than-expected net loss (EPS miss) and Retail-Flooring deterioration was worse than modeled. The unresolved PMW refinancing/credit overhang (the primary binary in the preview) remains the dominant negative for the stock.

Management reaffirmed the $45–50M FY26 guide (relief) but Q2 revenue missed the note's working estimate and key bridge metrics (H2 contracted revenue, cash, AR days) deteriorated, leaving guidance credibility weak — net-negative for a stock priced for a ramp.

Massive ARR miss (11.6M vs ~15.8–15.9M expected) and management withdrawing its year-end ARR growth target, plus deferred gift-card ARR, overwhelm modest revenue/EPS noise and trigger a strongly negative re-rating risk.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA materially beat the stale consensus and the note's base case, and management reaffirmed FY guides — clear positives. However gross margin compressed to low-30s (30.3%) and GAAP EPS missed materially, and the stock entered the print priced-for-perfection, leaving the overall read mixed-to-positive.

Revenue and adj. EPS printed essentially inline, but management cut FY guidance (notably adj. EBITDA), reported a meaningful adj. EBITDA miss, sharply lowered FCF, and disclosed far larger-than-expected center closures — a negative surprise for a stock that ran up into the print, so expect a strongly negative reaction.

Management secured a single registrational AA trial, confirmed ZENITH-AD starts (AD-3 by Sept) and showed a stronger-than-expected cash position / raised year-end cash guide, while the quarter’s royalty revenue missed modestly. The pipeline/regulatory clarity and reduced near-term dilution risk should drive a positive re-rate.

Headline revenue materially exceeded the note's model, but the beat was driven by a new gross presentation of ~$4.4M pass-through electricity (underlying revenue ~inline). The big ATM/cash raise and retired preferred shares materially de-risk the financing runway (positive), but a wider net loss, front-loaded Briscoe repair costs and heavy dilution are negatives — nets to a modestly positive relief reaction.

Normalized EBITDA and margins materially beat the key pre-release bar, ACV and pipeline came in much stronger than the turnaround story needed, and management engaged an advisor and raised the cost-savings target — these positives outweigh a modest revenue miss and point to relief for the equity stub.

Large headline revenue miss (procurement drop) will weigh, but the quarter showed encouraging mix (SI growth), meaningful gross-margin expansion, cash resilience and a reaffirmed 'toward the high end' EBITDA guide — a mixed print that should produce a modestly negative near-term reaction.

Revenue materially exceeded the pre-release build and consensus on much stronger realized oil pricing and higher volumes, and liquidity/leverage improved, but adjusted EBITDA came in below the note's target and production declined sequentially; management merely reiterated FY EBITDA guidance, so upside is real but muted by operational softness and positioning.

Quarter largely tracked the preview: pre-revenue, no material project financing, and a narrow cash runway ($0.5M) — but net loss and EPS were modestly better than my model and management reported meaningful post-quarter ATM proceeds (~$2.9M) plus draws on the B. Riley line, which materially reduce near-term delisting/extinction risk. Lack of a disclosed equity-deficit figure keeps uncertainty high.

Cash came in meaningfully above the preview (~$10.7M vs est. ~$9.5M) and management said it funds operations for at least one year, and PATHFINDER is fully funded; those relieve near-term dilution fears. Offsets: wider net loss, higher R&D, PATHFINDER enrollment slipped to Q4 and the pivotal ASPIRE still needs external funding.

Quarter missed revenue expectations but the print delivered a materially stronger balance sheet (cash $48.9M vs the $22–26M feared), a much-larger-than-expected mark on the Shougang JV stake (~$110M), and the reinstatement of full-year guidance — all of which materially reduce the dilution/runway risk and should drive a strong positive re-rate.

Revenue materially missed the preview/consensus (~$1.79M vs $0.836M), but the company secured ~$70M in commitments, set a $5 conversion floor and reaffirmed the 2,000-unit target — reducing immediate bankruptcy tail risk even as operational cadence and ASP/timing worries remain.

The only meaningful surprise was a modest raise to FY2026 cash spend (midpoint +10%), a negative for a stock trading near its high; that was partly offset by combined cash of ~$43M and management saying liquidity funds operations into 2028, so the print is slightly negative overall for a richly positioned name.

Revenue came in meaningfully above the thin consensus and, more importantly, gross profit was positive/roughly flat (an inflection vs prior negative quarters) while SG&A and operating cash flow improved — all relief relative to the base/bear scenarios. Offsetting this is a large increase in debt and the fact that ~$10M of cash is restricted (only ~$0.7M available), and management did not resolve the Nasdaq compliance binary on the call, leaving material event-driven risk intact.

Q2 revenue came in well below consensus and even beneath management's lower preliminary range, and the company cut FY26 guidance midpoint below the street; liquidity improved modestly via an ATM but remains tight, leaving the print net-negative for equity given the outstanding converts and cash runway concerns.
